cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here would be about sweep TIMING rather than about the defect. It must be read in-guest before it is called either way.

title: one duplicated string was stored into every interface the loop produced
object: the extcap tool's help string, one g_strdup
lifetime_ender: g_free(interface->help) in extcap_free_interface, for the FIRST interface holding the alias
shape: one allocation stored into several owners, each of which frees it
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is the SAME free for the second interface, which holds the identical pointer.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8:extcap.c carries `int_iter->help = g_strdup(help);` (`grep -c` = 1), with the duplication moved to the assignment. The form duplicating once outside the loop is at 07ffcf90426b^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.
nested_why: the object came straight from g_malloc / g_new / g_new0 / g_strdup / getline -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no wmem allocator between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../wmem-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the duplication is OUTSIDE the loop and the assignment INSIDE it, so a tool exposing N interfaces produces N owners of one string and N frees -- the fix swaps where the g_strdup happens rather than adding or removing a free. The number of frees is attacker-visible in the tool's own output.
